about.title: Winters Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription:
Winters is a small town, and a death here is rarely an abstraction. Public records for 2025 show 5 injury collisions in the city, 6 people hurt, and no traffic deaths, which is a fortunate year on paper. Still, families in Yolo County lose people to crashes on Grant Avenue and East Grant Avenue, on County Road 89 north of Niemann Street, on farm sites, in hospitals, and in ordinary places where someone failed to take basic care. Collisions in town tend to cluster on Friday mornings between 7 and 9 a.m., when people are heading to work or school.

A California wrongful death case is a civil action. It runs on its own track, apart from any criminal charges or police findings, and it exists so a family can recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. Our team handles wrongful death cases on a contingency basis, meaning you pay no fee unless we recover compensation for your family.

whyChoose.title: What Winters Families Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Standing Matters
items.desc: California limits who can bring a wrongful death claim: the spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. Our team can quickly confirm whether you have the right to file.

items.title: Two Years, Sometimes Less
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a city, county or other government entity is involved. Getting an early opinion protects that deadline.

items.title: Losses the Law Recognizes
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. We pursue these on a contingency basis with no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: There were no traffic deaths reported in Winters last year. Can I still have a wrongful death case?
items.answer: Yes. The 2025 public record shows zero traffic deaths in Winters, but wrongful death claims are not limited to car crashes or to a single year. Deaths on farms, in medical settings, on unsafe property, or on roads outside city limits in Yolo County can all give rise to a civil claim if negligence was involved.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do I have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action with its own standard of proof and its own deadline. Our team can move forward while the criminal case is pending, and the outcome of one does not decide the other.

items.question: Does it cost anything to speak with us about your case?
items.answer: No. There is no cost for your initial consultation. We work on a contingency basis, meaning we charge no fee unless your family recovers compensation, and your first conversation carries no obligation.
